newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine sells four tonnes germanium - govt agency.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine sells four tonnes germanium - govt agency.

text.p: Two unnamed companies won tenders to purchase four tonnes of germanium from a Ukrainian metals plant, the Ukrinform state news agency said on Tuesday.

The agency's weekly Business News magazine said that the Zaporizhya titanium-magnesium plant sold the metal for slightly less than the original asking price of $1550 per tonne, but did not state the final sale price.
"Payment for the germanium is expected within a week," the report said.
It said seven companies competed in the tender but did not say whether they were foreign or local.

The material was left over from an August 1996 sale of 6.5 tonnes, valued at $10.5 million, to three unnamed foreign firms -- including to a British company, which bought 2.5 tonnes at $1825 per kilogram.
The weekly reported previously that two of the companies, which won tenders to purchase and re-sell the metal, had failed to find buyers for the 4.33 tonnes for which they had contracted.
Germanium is a by-product of zinc and copper ores used in high-frequency and high-power electronic applications such as infra-red systems, fibre optics and semi-conductors.

Ukraine sold the metal from government reserves to raise money for modernisation of the plant, which requires about $15 million for a 12-month upgrade programme. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
